# One command answers two paused runs. The run of the second item sets the choice no, so it refuses the answer yes while the first run takes it, and the exit code is 1.
isolate

exec git init -q -b main origin
exec git -C origin add readme.txt
exec git -C origin -c user.name=e2e -c user.email=e2e@example.com commit -q -m start

subst config/projects/local.star

exec obeereal item add local ship-parent --title 'Parent' --body-file body.txt
exec obeereal run ship-parent local --workflow flow/fan.star &
waitstatus 'paused: Ship one?'
waitstatus 'paused: Ship two?'

# A selector that fits no run answers nothing.
! exec obeereal answer --all --question nothing yes
stderr 'no waiting run matches'

# The refusal of one run does not stop the other.
! exec obeereal answer --all yes
stdout -count=1 '\trefused: '
stdout -count=1 '\tanswered$'
stderr '1 of 2 runs did not take the answer'

# The run that refused still waits. A later answer in the shape that it accepts ends it.
exec obeereal status
stdout 'paused: Ship two\?'
exec obeereal answer --all --question 'Ship two' no
stdout -count=1 '\tanswered$'
wait

-- origin/readme.txt --
The source repository.
-- body.txt --
Ship them.
-- config/projects/local.star --
project(
    source      = "@WORK@/origin",
    base_branch = "main",
    gate        = "true",
    test_report = "r.xml",
)
-- flow/fan.star --
def ask(item):
    if item.title == "two":
        wait(name = "ask", question = "Ship two?", choices = ["no"])
    else:
        wait(name = "ask", question = "Ship %s?" % item.title)

def main(item):
    ids = []
    for title in ["one", "two"]:
        made = item_create(name = "create-" + title, key = title, title = title, body = title, parent = item.id)
        ids.append(made.id)
    runs = spawn(items = ids, entry = "ask", name = "fan")
    gather(runs, name = "fan")
